findings.source_passage: where every sword seems a flash of the Northern Lights, and the successive armed kings and Emperors dash by, like a charge of crowned centaurs
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Who Garnery the painter is'
findings.why_it_matters: This is the most quotable, rhetorically extravagant sentence in the chapter — the 'crowned centaurs' image is distinctively Melvillean hyperbole and the entire Versailles digression is condensed to a mere clause ('see Versailles' hall of battles'), erasing the voice-establishing simile entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full Versailles sentence with 'every sword seems a flash of the Northern Lights' and 'a charge of crowned centaurs'; this is the chapter's primary signature line and must appear verbatim or very close to it.

findings.source_passage: with the microscopic diligence of a Leuwenhoeck submits to the inspection of a shivering world ninety-six fac-similes of magnified Arctic snow crystals. I mean no disparagement to the excellent voyager (I honor him for a veteran), but in so important a matter it was certainly an oversight not to have procured for every crystal a sworn affidavit taken before a Greenland Justice of the Peace
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The natural aptitude of the French'
findings.why_it_matters: The Leeuwenhoek comparison and the mock-legal absurdity ('sworn affidavit taken before a Greenland Justice of the Peace') are a sustained satirical aside that defines the narrator's ironic register; the draft lists only the snow crystals without the surrounding voice, erasing Ishmael's comic persona entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the Leeuwenhoeck simile and the sworn-affidavit joke; these sentences are not mere facts but the chapter's signature ironic digression and must be preserved recognizably.

findings.source_passage: that rolls his black weedy bulk in the sea like some mossy rock-slide from the Patagonian cliffs. His jets are erect, full, and black like soot; so that from so abounding a smoke in the chimney, you would think there must be a brave supper cooking in the great bowels below
findings.why_it_matters: The chimney/supper simile ('brave supper cooking in the great bowels below') is a characteristic piece of Melvillean domestic-grotesque humor; the draft keeps 'jets erect and black as soot' but drops the second half of the image entirely, losing the comedic elaboration.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the chimney-supper simile after 'jets erect and black as soot'; it is brief enough to include without budget strain and carries significant voice weight.

findings.source_passage: causing the slight boat to rock in the swells like a skiff caught nigh the paddle-wheels of an ocean steamer. Thus, the foreground is all raging commotion; but behind, in admirable artistic contrast, is the glassy level of a sea becalmed
findings.why_it_matters: The steamer/paddle-wheel simile is an anachronistically modern intrusion that marks the passage's interpretive interest (the text's modernity self-consciousness); the draft omits it and softens the foreground/background contrast rhetoric.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'like a skiff caught nigh the paddle-wheels of an ocean steamer' and the explicit 'foreground raging commotion / behind glassy calm' antithesis, which the draft blurs.

findings.source_passage: picturesqueness of things seems to be peculiarly evinced in what paintings and engravings they have of their whaling scenes. With not one tenth of England's experience in the fishery, and not the thousandth part of that of the Americans, they have nevertheless furnished both nations with the only finished sketches at all capable of conveying the real spirit
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The natural aptitude of the French'
findings.why_it_matters: The opening of this paragraph — the diagnosis of French 'natural aptitude for the picturesqueness of things' — is the chapter's thesis statement about aesthetics and national character; the draft collapses it into a subordinate clause, losing the rhetorical structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the paragraph with the full 'natural aptitude for the picturesqueness of things' sentence before moving to the English/American contrast.

summary: Two high-severity losses — the 'crowned centaurs' / Versailles sentence and the Leeuwenhoek / Greenland-Justice-of-the-Peace satirical aside — erase the chapter's most memorable voice-defining moments and require regeneration.
